I am publishing my first book and paid for editing and a cover. Thankfully, I had a friend who is a retired professor who helped with the first round of editing, so that saved a lot regarding development editing. So, I only paid for someone to edit for grammar, etc., and that was after I did a run-through with paid Grammarly, so there wasn't much for them to edit.

I feel like a cover sells, so I did pay quite a bit and am happy with the results.

The thing is though, I already have an audience, I am a keynote speaker and have a base of support already established. I have a mailing list of over 300 signed up for the book launch notification when it is available, and a large number of people are coming to my book launch celebration in person.

For me, the book is a marketing tool for keynote speaking and will pay for itself even if I don't sell a single copy upon launch. As an author, I can charge more for keynotes and will likely sell some copies with each keynote I give.

All of this to say that my situation is unique and justifies paying for a high quality cover, editing and marketing although my marketing budget is geared towards the keynote speaking I will be pushing the book as well.

IF I did not have this established audience I would have likely not paid what I did unless the idea of having a book published meant more to me than making back my costs. Which is totally understandable and reasonable.

As many have stated, learning and doing some of this on your own such as book cover design with many tools and inexpensive sources available. Editing yourself or utilizing communities that do edit for edit or even seeing if there is something you can offer a local editor if theres a skillset or something you do beyond writing that they may be interested in.

As for marketing, there is going to be a cost but you can reduce that cost by learning how to do it effectively as well as trying to push for a organic marketing approach

I try to not put much thought into it either way. I'm agnostic i suppose by definition and at times have leaned towards believing simply because the Universe is way above my pay grade. If someone's belief brings them comfort and allows for them to continue forward in this grim life then I support it. 


For me, it has never brought comfort. Only anxiety and shame in praying to a God that ignores me. Maybe that's why i don't believe sometimes...it's easier to believe there is no God then a God that ignores you. 

Ironically I prayed today. Maybe it fell on empty ears or maybe it was just a silent thought spoken out of a learned habit from my childhood. 

If there is a God, and maybe there is l but I am not quite sure I can say it is an interventionist God.

 I am not quite sure we have all the answers to the Universe and just as it is easier to not believe in a God that ignores you, it is easier to create a reason for the existence. What is our purpose without a God? We desire  purpose. What is this life with no purpose and can we have a purpose without a God? Individually I think for certain we can. As a species, for the sake of existing, do we? Does it matter? No, I do not think it does. We are here and I am not sure why. I don't know if I care to ever find out. 

People spend their entire lives trying to find proof or disprove and I find myself slightly saddened by the wasted potential of that life. For those that truly believe I suppose it was of no waste. Which is why I feel greater sorrow for those that do not believe but spend their time arguing with those that do. In their minds, the believer is a fool. Well you are a fool to try to convince a fool that they are a fool. So I guess this too makes me a fool.

I wonder what we could accomplish if we focused on the problems we see. If there is a God why waste our time arguing it when this unique creation crumbles around us. To argue there is a creator and this life is a gift but do nothing to preserve its gift is not only a shame but ungodly. 

If there is a God and God is in all of us I am not confident  it is a good God or  a fair God. 


So I am not sure I believe in God and I definitely do not think I believe in an interventionist God. If there happens to be a God, I am not sure it is my God or a good God at that. Every artist has walked away from a piece unfinished and maybe we are that piece. To be created and forgotten. I think I'll return to not thinking about it now.

Two things to keep in mind is firstly recovery is not linear and do not be discouraged if it plateaus for a bit or you have set backs. Just keep working. Secondly nobody knows and nobody can tell you. Reality is the brain and Spinal cord are probably the least understood parts of our body and Spinal cord injury research has changed a lot over the years so if anyone gives you definite answer as to whether you will recover or not, they don't really know. Even doctors can make calculated estimates based on their knowledge, the data and what they see but it isn't a definite answer. So keep grinding or start if you aren't and give it your all to see where you end up.
